description: The plot titled “Hidden State Mean” illustrates the absolute mean values of hidden states across different layers of a model, comparing three distinct metrics: the hidden state mean before the gate, the hidden state mean after the gate, and the hidden state mean of a baseline. The x-axis, labeled “Layer,” uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to approximately 25, with tick labels appearing at intervals of 5, representing the layer index. The y-axis, labeled “Abs Mean,” uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to just over 4, with tick marks at intervals of 1. The blue dashed line, representing the hidden state mean before the gate with an average value of 0.71, remains relatively low and flat across layers 0 to 20, then sharply increases after layer 20, reaching a value of approximately 4.5 at layer 25. The orange dotted line, representing the hidden state mean after the gate with an average value of 0.05, stays consistently near zero throughout the entire layer range, fluctuating slightly between approximately 0 and 0.05. The green solid line, representing the hidden state mean of the baseline with an average value of 0.04, remains nearly flat and very close to zero across all layers, with values hovering just above zero, reaching a maximum of approximately 0.05 near layer 25.
